mainTopic: Honoring שבת, the power of answering אמן, and the sins that caused חורבן ירושלים
overview: This amud is a long chain of אגדה. It opens by finishing a story about a Sage who begged scholars not to neglect עונג שבת. The גמרא then teaches that even a יחיד must say ויכולו on Friday night, because this makes him a partner with הקב"ה in creation and brings blessings from the escorting angels. A good angel and a bad angel check whether the home is ready for שבת. Next come teachings about setting a table on ערב שבת and on מוצאי שבת, and the story of רבי אבהו's calf, which warns against being stingy in honoring שבת. The גמרא then praises answering אמן and אמן יהא שמיה רבא with full strength, and explains that אמן stands for אל מלך נאמן. Returning to שבת, it teaches that fires come from חילול שבת. This leads into a list of sins that caused חורבן ירושלים, including neglecting קריאת שמע, interrupting children's Torah learning, failing to rebuke, and disgracing תלמידי חכמים. Along the way there is a section on the great value of תינוקות של בית רבן. The amud ends with רבא's claim that trustworthy people had disappeared, and a challenge from רב קטינא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A Sage urges scholars not to neglect עונג שבת
steps.stepSummary: The end of a story: a Sage (רבי זירא, named on the previous amud) would go to pairs of scholars learning on שבת and beg them not to 'desecrate' שבת by skipping its enjoyment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would seek out pairs of Sages and say to them: Please, I beg you, do not desecrate it (שבת).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a list of stories about how great Sages honored שבת. This Sage pushed scholars to stop and enjoy שבת properly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we think of חילול שבת as doing forbidden work. Here the word is used in a softer sense: failing to give שבת its proper עונג is also a kind of 'desecration'. Even Torah learning should not fully crowd out the enjoyment of שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: pairs (here: pairs of scholars learning together)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Do not desecrate' here does not mean the scholars were doing forbidden מלאכה. It means not giving שבת its due enjoyment, for example by learning nonstop instead of eating and resting.

phrases.english: would go around to pairs and pairs of Sages,
phrases.notes: This is רבי זירא, who was mentioned on the previous amud.

phrases.english: he said to them:
Please, I beg of you,
do not desecrate it (Shabbat).
phrases.notes: By failing to delight in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְהַדַּר אַזּוּזֵי זוּזֵי דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of stories (on the previous amud) about how Sages honored שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neglecting the enjoyment of שבת is a form of 'desecrating' it.

steps.title: Even an individual must say ויכולו on Friday night
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יהושע בן לוי) rules that even someone praying alone on Friday night must recite ויכולו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was רבי יהושע בן לוי: Even an individual who prays on Friday night must say 'ויכולו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about Friday night davening. Even without a ציבור, a person must say ויכולו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think ויכולו is mainly a communal declaration, like testimony said together. This ruling makes it a duty for each person. The reason is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: the passage 'And the heavens and earth were finished' (בראשית ב:א-ג)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice of saying ויכולו on Friday night even when davening alone.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
Even an individual who prays on Shabbat eve
must say 'Vayechulu',

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ יָחִיד הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from stories about honoring שבת to a ruling about Friday night prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a יחיד must say ויכולו on Friday night.

steps.title: Saying ויכולו makes one a partner in Creation
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא explains why: whoever says ויכולו is treated as a partner of הקב"ה in creation, based on reading ויכולו as ויכלו.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב המנונא said: Anyone who prays on Friday night and says 'ויכולו', the verse treats him as if he became a partner with הקב"ה in the work of Creation. As it says 'וַיְכֻלּוּ' (they were finished). Do not read it 'וַיְכֻלּוּ' but 'וַיְכַלּוּ' (they finished).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind the previous ruling. Saying ויכולו is so valuable that every individual should do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וַיְכֻלּוּ means 'they were finished' (passive). The דרשה rereads it as וַיְכַלּוּ, 'they finished' (active, plural). So the one saying it and הקב"ה are pictured as 'finishing' creation together. Since this merit belongs to each person, even a יחיד needs to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: the verse credits him as if
do not read (a דרשה that rereads a word's vowels)

steps.confusionAlert: אל תקרי does not change the Torah's actual text or reading. It is a דרשה that draws an extra lesson from a possible alternate vocalization.

phrases.english: As Rav Hamnuna said:
Anyone who prays on Shabbat eve and says 'Vayechulu',
the verse credits him

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ נַעֲשָׂה שׁוּתָּף לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: as if he became a partner with the Holy One, Blessed be He,
in the work of Creation,
as it says: 'Vayechulu' (they were finished).
Do not read 'Vayechulu',
but rather 'Vayechallu' (they finished).
phrases.notes: The plural 'they' includes the person reciting it along with God.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the reason (the 'ד' of דאמר) for the ruling in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The ruling that even a יחיד must say ויכולו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב המנונא's דרשה on ויכולו / ויכלו (בראשית ב:א).

steps.title: Speech counts like action
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר shows from a פסוק that speaking counts like doing. This explains how just saying ויכולו can make a person a 'partner' in creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: From where do we know that speech is like action? As it says: 'By the word of God the heavens were made.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a hidden question: how can merely saying words make someone a partner in creation? The answer is that words count as deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heavens were made through God's speech, so speech itself is a form of action. Therefore, a person who declares ויכולו is treated as if he took part in the act of finishing creation.
steps.whatToRemember: Saying ויכולו, even alone, makes one a 'partner' in creation, because speech counts as action ("בִּדְבַר ה׳ שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ").

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know that speech is like action?
As it says: 'By the word of God the heavens were made' (Psalms 33:6).

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִין שֶׁהַדִּיבּוּר כְּמַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the idea in step 3 that saying words can count as taking part in creation.
steps.raayaObject: The principle that speech is like action.

steps.title: Angels bless one who says ויכולו with atonement
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא in the name of מר עוקבא: the two מלאכי השרת who accompany a person place their hands on his head and say his sins are forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: Anyone who prays on Friday night and says 'ויכולו', the two ministering angels who escort a person place their hands on his head and say to him: 'Your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another reward for saying ויכולו: the person's escorting angels bless him with כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 gave a reward in terms of status (partner in creation). This step adds a personal reward, forgiveness of sins. The angels quote ישעיהו ו:ז, the words an angel spoke when purifying ישעיהו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said in the name of Mar Ukva:
Anyone who prays on Shabbat eve and says 'Vayechulu',
the two ministering angels
who escort a person
place their hands on his head
and say to him:
'Your iniquity is removed, and your sin is atoned' (Isaiah 6:7).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second reward for saying ויכולו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who says ויכולו on Friday night is blessed by his angels with כפרה.

steps.title: The good angel and the bad angel inspect the Shabbat home
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי בר יהודה: a good angel and a bad angel escort a person home from shul on Friday night. Whatever they find there, the same state is blessed to continue next שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: Two ministering angels escort a person on Friday night from the synagogue to his home, one good and one bad. When he comes home and finds a lamp lit, a table set, and his bed made, the good angel says: 'May it be Your will that it be like this next שבת,' and the bad angel is forced to answer 'אמן.' If not, the bad angel says: 'May it be Your will that it be like this next שבת,' and the good angel is forced to answer 'אמן.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא continuing the theme of angels on Friday night. It shows the power of a home properly prepared for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same blessing ('may next שבת be like this') is a blessing or a curse depending on what the home looks like. A prepared home forces even the bad angel to agree to a good future. An unprepared home forces even the good angel to agree to more of the same neglect.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source of the custom of singing שלום עליכם to the escorting angels on Friday night.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת מְלַוִּין לוֹ לְאָדָם
phrases.english: Two ministering angels escort a person
on Shabbat eve from the synagogue to his home,
one good and one bad.
When he comes home and finds a lamp lit,
a table set, and his bed made,
the good angel says:
'May it be Your will that it be like this for another Shabbat,'
and the bad angel answers 'Amen' against his will.
And if not (the home is not prepared),
the bad angel says:
'May it be Your will that it be like this for another Shabbat,'
and the good angel answers 'Amen' against his will.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of the escorting angels from step 5, now focused on how the home is prepared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A home prepared for שבת brings a blessing that it continue. An unprepared home brings the opposite.

steps.title: Always set a full table on ערב שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר: one should always set his table nicely on ערב שבת, even if he only needs a כזית of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: A person should always set his table on ערב שבת, even if he needs only a כזית of food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the 'set table' in the ברייתא to a practical teaching: set a respectable table for שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is honoring שבת, not filling one's stomach. Even if you are not hungry and will eat only a כזית, the table should be set as for an important meal.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר אָדָם שֻׁלְחָנוֹ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A person should always set his table on Shabbat eve,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לִכְזַיִת.
phrases.english: even if he needs only an olive's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר אָדָם שֻׁלְחָנוֹ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'שולחן ערוך' of the ברייתא in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Set a full table for שבת even for a small amount of food.

steps.title: Also set a table on מוצאי שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא: one should also set his table on מוצאי שבת, even for only a כזית, to escort שבת out with honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חנינא said: A person should always set his table on מוצאי שבת, even if he needs only a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: Parallel to the previous teaching, the גמרא says שבת should be honored with a set table on the way out too, not only on the way in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a king is escorted both when he arrives and when he leaves, שבת is honored at its departure. This is the source for the מלוה מלכה meal.

keyTerms.meaning: the night after שבת ends (Saturday night)
the meal 'escorting the queen' on Saturday night

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for eating a מלוה מלכה meal on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר אָדָם שֻׁלְחָנוֹ בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: A person should always set his table on Motzaei Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ אֶלָּא לִכְזַיִת.
phrases.english: even if he needs only an olive's worth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר אָדָם שֻׁלְחָנוֹ בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 7, applying the same idea to the end of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Set a table on מוצאי שבת too, even for a small amount.

steps.title: Hot water and warm bread after Shabbat are healing
steps.stepSummary: Hot water and warm bread on מוצאי שבת are a remedy (מלוגמא).
steps.simpleTranslation: Hot water on מוצאי שבת is a remedy; warm bread on מוצאי שבת is a remedy.
steps.whatsHappening: Continuing the topic of the מוצאי שבת meal, the גמרא notes that freshly heated water and bread after שבת are healthy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת one cannot cook or bake, so food is not freshly heated. Right after שבת, fresh hot water and warm bread are especially beneficial, which encourages preparing them for the מוצאי שבת meal.

phrases.english: Hot water on Motzaei Shabbat is a remedy;
warm bread on Motzaei Shabbat is a remedy.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַמִּין בְּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת — מְלוּגְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail about what is good to eat at the מוצאי שבת meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hot water and warm bread after שבת are beneficial.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's calf and the danger of cutting corners
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו had a calf slaughtered every מוצאי שבת but ate only a kidney. His son אבימי suggested saving a kidney from ערב שבת instead. They spared the calf, and a lion ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי אבהו, on מוצאי שבת, they would prepare a choice third-born calf, and he would eat one kidney from it. When his son אבימי grew up, he said to him: Why waste so much? Let us leave a kidney over from ערב שבת. They spared it, and a lion came and ate it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this section with a story showing that being stingy in honoring the מוצאי שבת meal leads to loss, not savings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימי's idea sounded sensible: why slaughter a whole calf for one kidney? But by skipping the special מוצאי שבת preparation, they lost the entire calf to a lion. Money spent honoring שבת is not wasted, and 'saving' on it can cost more.

keyTerms.meaning: a choice calf (third-born, or in its third year)

steps.whatToRemember: Honor שבת generously at both ends: say ויכולו, have the home ready, set a table on ערב שבת and on מוצאי שבת. Cutting corners on honoring שבת does not truly save anything.

phrases.english: For Rabbi Abahu they would prepare
on Motzaei Shabbat a choice third-born calf,
and he would eat one kidney from it.
When his son Avimi grew up,
he said to him:
Why waste so much?
Let us leave a kidney over from Shabbat eve.
They spared it, and a lion came and ate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ הֲוָה עָבְדִין לֵיהּ בְּאַפּוֹקֵי שַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates step 8, the importance of the מוצאי שבת meal, through a story.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One should not be stingy in honoring שבת, including the meal on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: Answering 'אמן יהא שמיה רבא' with full strength tears up a harsh decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches that whoever answers אמן יהא שמיה רבא מברך with all his strength has his harsh heavenly decree torn up. He proves it from a פסוק in שירת דבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Anyone who answers 'Amen, may His great name be blessed' with all his strength has his decree torn up. The פסוק says: 'When punishments are annulled in Israel, when the people offer themselves, bless ה׳.' Why were the punishments annulled? Because they blessed ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the reward for honoring שבת to the reward for answering אמן יהא שמיה רבא. רבי יהושע בן לוי says a person who answers it with full strength has his bad decree cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from reading the פסוק as cause and effect. The punishments were annulled (בפרוע פרעות) because the people blessed ה׳‎ (ברכו ה׳). Answering יהא שמיה רבא is a way of blessing ה׳, so it brings the same result.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Amen, may His great name be blessed', the congregation's response in קדיש
With all his strength, meaning with full heart and focus
They tear up his sentence, so a harsh heavenly decree is cancelled

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן יְהֵא שְׁמֵיהּ רַבָּא מְבָרַךְ״
phrases.english: Anyone who answers 'Amen, may His great name be blessed'
with all his strength,
phrases.notes: רש"י understands this as full concentration, not necessarily a loud voice.

phrases.english: they tear up his sentence (decree) for him,
as it says: 'When punishments are annulled in Israel
when the people offer themselves, bless ה׳.'
What is the reason for 'when punishments are annulled'?
Because they 'blessed ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: כׇּל הָעוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the reward for honoring שבת to a related topic, the reward for answering אמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answering אמן יהא שמיה רבא with full strength cancels a harsh heavenly decree.

steps.title: Even a trace of idolatry is forgiven
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא in the name of רבי יוחנן adds that even someone with a trace of עבודה זרה is forgiven. He learns it from a גזירה שוה linking 'פרעות' to 'פרוע', a word used about the חטא העגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even if he has a trace of idol worship in him, he is forgiven. It says here 'בפרוע פרעות', and it says there, about the Golden Calf, 'כי פרוע הוא' (the people were wild).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes the reward of the previous step even bigger: answering אמן brings forgiveness even for a trace of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a word link. The root פרע appears in our פסוק and also in the story of the עגל, where the people were 'פרוע', wild in idol worship. Since the same word is used, the 'annulled punishment' covers even that kind of sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A trace or hint of idol worship
It is written here... and it is written there, the standard way of linking two פסוקים by a shared word
Wild or unrestrained, said of the people at the עגל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ שֶׁמֶץ שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה —
phrases.english: Even if he has in him a trace of idol worship,
they forgive him.
It is written here: 'When punishments (פרעות) are annulled,'
and it is written there: 'For it (the nation) was wild (פרוע).'
phrases.notes: שמות לב:כה, about the חטא העגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same פסוק and widens the reward to include forgiveness for idolatry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answering אמן יהא שמיה רבא wholeheartedly brings forgiveness even for a trace of עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Answering אמן with full strength opens the gates of גן עדן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that whoever answers אמן with all his strength has the gates of גן עדן opened for him. He reads 'שומר אמונים' as 'שאומרים אמן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Anyone who answers 'Amen' with all his strength has the gates of גן עדן opened for him. The פסוק says: 'Open the gates, and a righteous nation that keeps faith (שומר אמונים) shall enter.' Do not read 'שומר אמונים' but 'שאומרים אמן', those who say Amen.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives another reward, this time for any אמן and not only אמן יהא שמיה רבא: the gates of גן עדן open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses an אל תיקרי, a playful re-reading of the letters of the פסוק. 'שומר אמונים' sounds like 'שאומרים אמן', so the righteous nation that enters the gates is the one that answers אמן.

keyTerms.meaning: They open the gates of גן עדן for him
Do not read it as... but as..., a re-reading of a פסוק for a דרשה

steps.confusionAlert: An אל תיקרי does not mean the פסוק is spelled wrong. The written text stays the same. The re-reading adds a second layer of meaning on top of the simple one.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Anyone who answers 'Amen' with all his strength,
they open the gates of Gan Eden for him,
as it says: 'Open the gates,
and a righteous nation that keeps faith shall enter.'
Do not read 'who keeps faith (shomer emunim)'
but rather 'who say Amen (she'omrim amen).'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּל הָעוֹנֶה ״אָמֵן״ בְּכׇל כֹּחוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel statement that adds a different reward for answering אמן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Answering אמן with all one's strength opens the gates of גן עדן.

steps.title: What does the word אמן stand for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word אמן hints to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'אמן'?
steps.whatsHappening: After all this praise of אמן, the גמרא asks what the word itself means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a challenge. It is a real request for information, asking what idea is packed into the word אמן.

phrases.english: What is 'Amen'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אָמֵן״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the key word of the previous statements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning or hint behind the word אמן.

steps.title: אמן stands for 'God, faithful King'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא explains that אמן is an abbreviation of אל מלך נאמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: 'God, faithful King' (אל מלך נאמן).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא answers that the letters א-מ-ן stand for אל מלך נאמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying אמן is therefore a short statement of faith that ה׳ is a King who can be trusted. That explains why it carries such great reward.

keyTerms.meaning: God, faithful King, the hidden meaning of the letters of אמן

steps.whatToRemember: Answering אמן wholeheartedly is a declaration of faith in ה׳ as faithful King. It tears up harsh decrees, brings forgiveness, and opens the gates of גן עדן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
'God, faithful King.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: ״אֵל מֶלֶךְ נֶאֱמָן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמן is an acronym of אל מלך נאמן.

steps.title: Fires break out where שבת is desecrated
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב יהודה son of רב שמואל, teaches that fire is found only where there is חילול שבת. He proves it from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה son of רב שמואל said in the name of רב: Fire is found only in a place where שבת is desecrated. The פסוק says: 'If you do not listen to Me to make שבת holy and not carry a load... I will set fire to its gates, and it will consume the palaces of ירושלים and will not be put out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to שבת, now from the side of punishment. רב says fires come because of חילול שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself links the two ideas. If they do not keep שבת, especially by carrying loads, ה׳ will set a fire in the gates. So fire is presented as a fitting punishment for desecrating שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: And I will kindle a fire

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda son of Rav Shmuel said in the name of Rav:
Fire is not found
except in a place where there is desecration of Shabbat,
as it says: 'And if you do not listen to Me
to sanctify the day of Shabbat
and not to carry a load, etc.,
then I will kindle a fire in its gates
and it will consume the palaces of Jerusalem and will not be extinguished.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: אֵין הַדְּלֵיקָה מְצוּיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of אמן and returns to שבת, focusing on the punishment for desecrating it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fires occur only where שבת is desecrated.

steps.title: What does 'it will not be extinguished' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the phrase 'ולא תכבה' in the פסוק adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and it will not be extinguished' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the last words of the פסוק, 'and it will not be put out'. This sets up רב נחמן בר יצחק's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every fire is put out in the end, so the phrase seems hard to understand. The גמרא wants to know what it is actually describing.

keyTerms.meaning: And it will not be extinguished

phrases.english: What is 'and it will not be extinguished'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״וְלֹא תִכְבֶּה״?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the פסוק quoted in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'ולא תכבה', since fires do eventually go out.

steps.title: The fire breaks out when no one is around to put it out
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the fire breaks out at a time when no people are around to put it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: At a time when there are no people around to put it out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'will not be put out' means the fire will start when nobody is there to fight it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase does not describe a magical fire that cannot be put out. It describes the timing of the punishment: the fire comes when no help is available, so it spreads.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
At a time when people are not
around to extinguish it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fire starts at a time when no one is present to put it out.

steps.title: ירושלים was destroyed because of חילול שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי teaches that ירושלים was destroyed only because its people desecrated שבת. He brings a פסוק from יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: ירושלים was destroyed only because they desecrated שבת in it. The פסוק says: 'They hid their eyes from My שבתות, and I was profaned among them.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes the theme further: חילול שבת caused not just fires but the whole destruction of ירושלים. This opens a list of opinions about why ירושלים was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל comes in a passage of rebuke right before the destruction. Ignoring שבת is listed as the cause of ה׳ being 'profaned' among them, which led to the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: ירושלים was destroyed only because of..., the formula repeated throughout this list
They hid (closed) their eyes, meaning they ignored

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Jerusalem was not destroyed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁחִלְּלוּ בָּהּ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: except because they desecrated Shabbat in it,
as it says: 'And from My Shabbatot they hid their eyes,
and I was profaned among them.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands רב's link between חילול שבת and fire into a link with the full destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורבן ירושלים was caused by חילול שבת.

steps.title: ירושלים was destroyed because they neglected קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says ירושלים was destroyed because people skipped קריאת שמע morning and evening. He uses three פסוקים from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: ירושלים was destroyed only because they neglected קריאת שמע morning and evening. The פסוק says: 'Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase strong drink...' and: 'There are harp and lute, drum and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they do not look at the work of ה׳,' and: 'Therefore My people goes into exile for lack of knowledge.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different reason for the destruction: people stopped saying קריאת שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works in three steps. First, morning and evening were filled with drinking. Second, during those parties they ignored ה׳. These are exactly the times for קריאת שמע. Third, 'therefore My people goes into exile' shows this was the cause of the גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Saying the שמע in the morning and in the evening

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because
they neglected the reading of Shema morning and evening,
as it says: 'Woe to those who rise early in the morning
to pursue strong drink, etc.,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו ה:יא. The rest of the פסוק mentions late in the evening.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And there are lyre and lute, drum and flute
and wine at their feasts,
but the work of ה׳ they do not look at,'
and it is written: 'Therefore My people is exiled for lack of knowledge.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another cause for the destruction alongside אביי's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורבן ירושלים was caused by neglecting קריאת שמע morning and evening.

steps.title: ירושלים was destroyed because children's Torah learning was stopped
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says ירושלים was destroyed because schoolchildren's Torah learning was stopped. He reads 'pour out on the child in the street' as cause and effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: ירושלים was destroyed only because they stopped the schoolchildren from learning. The פסוק says: 'Pour it out on the child in the street...' Why 'pour out' (the anger)? Because the child is in the street, not learning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives another cause: children were taken out of Torah learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק the same way as step 11, as cause and effect. ה׳'s anger is 'poured out' because the children are 'in the street' instead of in the בית מדרש learning Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: Schoolchildren learning Torah with their teacher

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבִּיטְּלוּ בָּהּ תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן,
phrases.english: they interrupted the schoolchildren in it (from learning),
as it says: 'Pour it on the child in the street, etc.'
What is the reason for 'pour out'?
Because the 'child is in the street.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another entry in the list of causes for the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורבן ירושלים was caused by stopping children's Torah learning.

steps.title: ירושלים was destroyed because people had no shame before each other
steps.stepSummary: עולא says ירושלים was destroyed because people felt no shame before one another, as the פסוק describes them doing abominations without embarrassment.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: ירושלים was destroyed only because people had no shame before one another. The פסוק says: 'They should be ashamed, for they did abominations, yet they are not ashamed at all...'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a reason based on character: people sinned openly with no embarrassment in front of others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says they did disgusting acts and were not even ashamed. Once shame is gone, nothing holds people back from sin, and that led to the destruction.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לָהֶם בּוֹשֶׁת פָּנִים זֶה מִזֶּה,
phrases.english: they had no shame before one another,
as it says: 'They acted shamefully, for they did abomination;
yet they are not ashamed at all, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another entry in the list of causes for the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורבן ירושלים was caused by a loss of shame before one another.

steps.title: ירושלים was destroyed because small and great were treated as equals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says ירושלים was destroyed because ordinary people and great people were treated as equal, so leaders were not given proper respect. The next פסוק describes the land's desolation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: ירושלים was destroyed only because small and great were made equal. The פסוק says: 'And the people shall be like the כהן,' and right after it is written: 'The land shall be completely emptied.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives another reason in this list: people did not honor their great leaders above ordinary people. The list continues with more reasons in steps 24, 25, and 35.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק describes a society where the common person is treated like the כהן, with no respect for greatness. The very next פסוק describes the land being destroyed, and the גמרא reads this order as cause and effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Small and great were made equal
And it is written right after it
It will be utterly emptied (made desolate)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא lists many causes for חורבן ירושלים: חילול שבת, neglecting קריאת שמע, stopping children's Torah learning, shamelessness, failing to honor great people, and, in the next steps, failing to rebuke one another, disgracing תלמידי חכמים, and the loss of trustworthy people. Each one is supported by a פסוק that connects the sin to the punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: These opinions do not really argue with each other. Each אמורא points to one sin that was a cause, and they can all be true together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because
the small and the great were made equal,
as it says: 'And the people shall be like the priest,'
and it is written after it: 'The land shall be utterly emptied.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another entry in the list of causes for the destruction; more follow in steps 24, 25 and 35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חורבן ירושלים was caused by treating ordinary people and great leaders as equals.

steps.title: Destroyed because no one rebuked anyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says ירושלים was destroyed because people did not rebuke one another, and he learns it from the image of grazing stags.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם, son of רבי שמעון בר אבא, said in the name of his father, who said in the name of רבי חנינא: ירושלים was destroyed only because people did not rebuke one another. The פסוק says: 'Her officers were like stags that found no pasture.' Stags graze with one's head next to the other's tail. In the same way, the Jews of that generation kept their faces down to the ground and did not rebuke one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another reason to the list of why ירושלים was destroyed: nobody corrected anybody else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא reads the stag image as a picture of behavior. Each stag faces the other's tail, so no one looks anyone in the face. The people did the same, looking away instead of correcting one another.

keyTerms.meaning: They pressed their faces to the ground, meaning they looked away

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Rav Amram, son of Rabbi Shimon bar Abba, said,
Rabbi Shimon bar Abba said,
Rabbi Chanina said:
Jerusalem was not destroyed

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁלֹּא הוֹכִיחוּ זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: except because they did not rebuke one another,
as it says: 'Her officers were like stags'
'that found no pasture.'
Just as with this stag,

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד זְנָבוֹ שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: the head of one is beside the tail of the other,
phrases.notes: When they graze, they do not face each other.

phrases.english: so too the Jews of that generation
pressed their faces to the ground
and did not rebuke one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another item to the list of reasons for the חורבן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים was destroyed because people failed to rebuke one another.

steps.title: Destroyed because Torah scholars were disrespected
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says ירושלים was destroyed because people disrespected the תלמידי חכמים, and he brings a פסוק from דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: ירושלים was destroyed only because people disgraced the Torah scholars in it. The פסוק says: 'They mocked the messengers of God, scorned His words, and taunted His prophets, until God's anger rose against His people, until there was no cure.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another reason for the destruction is given: people disrespected the תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'messengers of God' and 'His prophets' as including Torah scholars. The פסוק links mocking them directly to God's anger and a destruction that could not be healed.

keyTerms.meaning: They disgraced or treated with contempt

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because
they disgraced the Torah scholars in it,
as it says: 'They mocked the messengers of God'
'and scorned His words'
'and taunted His prophets,'
'until God's anger rose against His people'
'until there was no cure.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁבִּיזּוּ בָּהּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of reasons for the חורבן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים was destroyed because the תלמידי חכמים were disgraced.

steps.title: What does 'until there was no cure' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the closing words of רבי יהודה's פסוק mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'until there was no cure' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on the last words of the פסוק and asks what they mean. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'no cure' sounds extra, so the גמרא wants to know what it adds. The answer will connect it to people who disrespect scholars.

phrases.english: What is 'until there was no cure'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״עַד לְאֵין מַרְפֵּא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the previous step's פסוק

steps.title: One who disgraces scholars has no cure
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that anyone who disgraces תלמידי חכמים has no healing for his wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who disgraces Torah scholars has no healing for his wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: 'no cure' means that a person who disgraces scholars cannot be healed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב turns the phrase into a general rule that applies to any individual, not only to that generation. The punishment for disgracing scholars is described as incurable.
steps.whatToRemember: Disrespecting תלמידי חכמים is described as a wound with no cure.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Anyone who disgraces Torah scholars
has no healing for his wound.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'No cure' means that one who disgraces scholars has no healing for his wound.

steps.title: 'My anointed' are schoolchildren and 'My prophets' are scholars
steps.stepSummary: רב reads the פסוק 'Do not touch My anointed ones' as referring to schoolchildren and Torah scholars.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: What does the פסוק 'Do not touch My anointed ones, and do My prophets no harm' mean? 'Do not touch My anointed ones' means the schoolchildren. 'Do My prophets no harm' means the Torah scholars.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the theme of honoring Torah people, רב explains a פסוק so that it protects schoolchildren and scholars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Schoolchildren are called 'anointed,' meaning precious like kings. Scholars are compared to prophets. This sets up the next statements about how valuable children's learning is.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
What is the meaning of what is written:
'Do not touch My anointed ones, and do My prophets no harm'?
'Do not touch My anointed ones':
these are the schoolchildren;
'and do My prophets no harm':
these are the Torah scholars.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״אַל תִּגְּעוּ בִּמְשִׁיחָי וּבִנְבִיאַי אַל תָּרֵעוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same chain of tradition (רב יהודה אמר רב) and opens a related topic: honoring Torah learners
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Schoolchildren and Torah scholars are under God's special protection.

steps.title: The world exists because of children's Torah breath
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש, in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה, says the world exists only because of the breath of schoolchildren learning Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: The world continues to exist only because of the breath of schoolchildren learning Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues praising schoolchildren and says their Torah learning keeps the whole world going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Breath' (הבל) means the words of Torah the children recite. This is a very strong claim, and it will lead רב פפא to ask about adults' learning.

keyTerms.meaning: Breath, meaning the spoken words of Torah

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
The world does not exist
except because of the breath
of the schoolchildren.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the praise of schoolchildren
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world exists because of the Torah learning of schoolchildren.

steps.title: What about the learning of adults like us?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי why the learning of adults like themselves does not count the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: What about my learning and yours?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is surprised: if children's breath holds up the world, what about the Torah learning of great scholars like him and אביי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adults learn more and understand more deeply. So why give the credit only to children? This question sets up אביי's answer.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Mine and yours, what about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּידִי וְדִידָךְ מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the scope of step 29
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why adults' Torah learning does not sustain the world the way children's does

steps.title: Breath without sin is different
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that children's breath is free of sin, while adults' breath is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Breath that has sin in it is not like breath that has no sin in it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains what makes children's learning special: their words come from mouths that have not sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not the amount or depth of the learning but its purity. Adults have sins, so their Torah breath is not completely pure like children's.
steps.whatToRemember: Children's Torah is uniquely powerful because it is free of sin.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הֶבֶל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֵטְא
phrases.english: Breath that has sin in it is not like
breath that has no sin in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה הֶבֶל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Children's Torah breath is sinless, so it is greater than adults' breath.

steps.title: Do not stop children's learning, even to build the בית המקדש
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש teaches that schoolchildren may not be taken away from learning, even to build the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש also said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: We do not take schoolchildren away from their learning, even to build the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a practical rule showing how important children's learning is: nothing interrupts it, not even building the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building the בית המקדש is a huge מצוה, and it is still not a reason to stop children's Torah learning. This shows how much weight their learning carries.
steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes a well-known principle about the priority of children's Torah education.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְבַטְּלִין תִּינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן
phrases.english: We do not interrupt schoolchildren
even for building the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second statement of ריש לקיש in the same name
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Children's Torah learning is not interrupted even for building the בית המקדש.

steps.title: A city without schoolchildren is destroyed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש tells רבי יהודה נשיאה a tradition that a city with no schoolchildren learning Torah is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יהודה נשיאה: This is what I received from my ancestors (and some say: from your ancestors): Any city that has no schoolchildren learning Torah is destroyed.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש quotes an old tradition: a city without children learning Torah will be destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to the main theme of why cities like ירושלים are destroyed. There are two versions of whose ancestors the tradition came from, but the content is the same.

keyTerms.meaning: I have received as a tradition

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the word here is 'to' רבי יהודה נשיאה (לרבי), not 'in the name of' him. ריש לקיש is speaking directly to him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
This is what I received from my ancestors,
and some say: from your ancestors:
Any city that does not have in it
schoolchildren
they destroy it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ מְקּוּבְּלַנִי מֵאֲבוֹתַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ריש לקיש teaching about schoolchildren
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A city without schoolchildren learning Torah is destroyed.

steps.title: רבינא's version: the city is made desolate
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a slightly different wording: such a city is made desolate instead of destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: They make it desolate.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different version of the last word of the tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of מחריבין ('destroy it'), רבינא says מחרימין ('declare it banned' or 'leave it desolate'). The idea is similar, but the consequence is described differently.

keyTerms.meaning: They place it under a ban or leave it desolate

steps.whatToRemember: Whether the city is 'destroyed' or 'made desolate,' a city without children learning Torah has no future.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
They make it desolate.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: מַחְרִימִין אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Alternative wording of the consequence in step 33
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Such a city is made desolate (מחרימין).

steps.title: Destroyed because trustworthy people disappeared
steps.stepSummary: רבא says ירושלים was destroyed because there were no more trustworthy people (אנשי אמנה) left, citing ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: ירושלים was destroyed only because trustworthy people were gone from it. The פסוק says: 'Roam the streets of ירושלים and look, search its squares, and see if you can find a man who acts justly and seeks honesty, and I will forgive it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the list of reasons for the destruction. רבא blames the loss of honest, trustworthy people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק implies that even one honest person would have saved the city. Since it was destroyed, רבא concludes that no such person could be found.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
Jerusalem was destroyed only because
trustworthy people ceased from it,
as it says: 'Roam the streets of Jerusalem'
'and see, and know, and search its squares,'
'whether you can find a man' (whether there is a man)
'who acts justly, who seeks honesty,'
'and I will forgive it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא חָרְבָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁפָּסְקוּ מִמֶּנָּה אַנְשֵׁי אֲמָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of reasons for the חורבן after the side discussion about schoolchildren
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ירושלים was destroyed because no trustworthy people remained.

steps.title: But רב קטינא says trustworthy people never disappeared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא from רב קטינא, who says that even as ירושלים fell, trustworthy people were still there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב קטינא said: Even when ירושלים was failing, trustworthy people did not disappear from it. The פסוק says: 'When a man will grab his brother of his father's house, saying: You have a garment, be our leader.' This means: the things people cover up like a garment (secrets) are in your hands, so you are trusted. 'And let this ruin be under your hand,'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's statement: another אמורא says trustworthy people did still exist then. The explanation of the second half of the פסוק continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא reads 'you have a garment' as 'people's secrets are safe with you,' which describes a trustworthy person whom others want as their leader. If such people existed even at the time of the fall, how can רבא say they had disappeared? The גמרא then starts to explain 'this ruin under your hand,' and the explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: The 'garment' here is not about clothes. רב קטינא reads it as secrets people keep covered, which shows the person is trusted.

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But didn't Rav Ketina say:
Even at the time of Jerusalem's downfall
trustworthy people did not cease from it,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי יִתְפֹּשׂ אִישׁ בְּאָחִיו בֵּית אָבִיו
phrases.english: as it says: 'When a man grabs his brother of his father's house,'
'saying: You have a garment,'
'be a leader for us,'

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרִים שֶׁבְּנֵי אָדָם מִתְכַּסִּין בָּהֶן כְּשִׂמְלָה
phrases.english: things that people cover themselves with like a garment
are in your hands.
'And let this ruin be under your hand,'
phrases.notes: The explanation of this phrase continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רַב קַטִּינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's statement in step 35
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that אנשי אמנה had disappeared from ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב קטינא, based on a פסוק in ישעיהו, says trustworthy people remained even at the time of the downfall, which directly contradicts רבא.
